- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day avg) with negative sentiment, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 3–5 days (especially after spikes), shift forecast horizon slightly backward by 1–2 days to align with observed lag.  
- When sentiment turns positive after prolonged negativity, model often underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion speed — if history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 day pullback), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid premature normalization.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate downward risk — add 2–3% upward bias to counteract pessimism.
